analysis.purpose: The Rust structural parser: turns the token stream into a declaration tree (mod, struct, enum, trait, impl, fn, method, type alias, macro) plus a flat list of call sites, deliberately stopping short of a full expression parser because the symbol graph only needs declaration spans, nesting, and call-site heads.
responsibilities: Descend the token stream tolerantly, emitting a declaration per construct
Record nesting so members carry qualified names and member-of edges
Collect call sites in a separate whole-stream pass
Degrade on malformed input by skipping the construct rather than throwing
Extract trait default and required functions alike, without using body presence to distinguish them

businessRules.rule: Not a full expression parser — a tolerant brace/indent-level descent is enough, and is far less surface area to get wrong.
businessRules.rationale: The symbol graph needs spans, nesting and call heads; parsing expressions would add risk without adding graph value.

businessRules.rule: Struct fields, enum variants, const/static items and use statements are not symbols; their call sites are still collected.
businessRules.rationale: Altitude parity with the Java extractor.

businessRules.rule: macro_rules! bodies are skipped as a brace block rather than descended.
businessRules.rationale: An honest, documented limitation — macro bodies are not ordinary Rust syntax.
